title: Vulcain/Volvo S1 separation-similarity benchmark
description: Ostlund Vulcain/S1/S3 similarity case for wall Mach, wall pressure, pressure-gradient, and separation/side-load relevance. This case is report-only for pressure and separation physics until boundary-layer and side-load models are available.

source.citation: Ostlund, J. Supersonic Flow Separation with Application to Rocket Engine Nozzles.
references: Section 10.3: S1 and S3 scaling of Vulcain nozzle flow
Table 7: main characteristics of Vulcain, S1, and S3
Figures 94-99: wall and internal flow comparisons
Discussion of wall-pressure gradient and side-load sensitivity
source.notes: The S1 air model is used here because its table provides complete dimensions and gamma=1.4-compatible gas assumptions.

ideal_exit_mach.source_ref: Section 10.3: air Mach 5 reached near area ratio 25

curves.axis_calibration: normalized S1 wall-pressure trace, hand-digitized trend
normalized S1 wall-Mach trace, hand-digitized trend

expected_physics_gaps: Wall-pressure gradient and separation/side-load behavior require boundary-layer and shock/separation models beyond the current quasi-1D wall-pressure estimate.
Similarity of internal Mach contours cannot be validated until the MOC field is benchmarked against published flowfield contours.
The benchmark is evidence for downstream CFD/thermal/structural review, not hardware qualification.
